title: Moving-source field consistency: what survives of the wake
headline: Delayed-center construction is not a Poisson-vacuum exterior. Branch C written explicitly (three breaking parameters) and closed: the dissipative parameter that makes the dipole makes a first-order self-acceleration the solar-system ephemeris floor excludes. Converged with the boost-invariant control.

claims.claim: For \(\lvert\beta_g\rvert<1\), the delayed-center potential with \(\boldsymbol{\Delta}(R)=-\mathbf{w}R/c_g\) has a convergent Legendre expansion whose angular shape is radius-independent and whose \(n\ge1\) terms are forbidden by the standard exterior Laplace equation
claims.evidence: Closed-form derivation in § The delayed-center potential is not a Poisson-vacuum field; identity checked numerically to \(10^{-8}\), but the check is uncataloged and therefore not yet admissible under the house rule
claims.kill: Catalog the negative-control fixture; algebra is done.

claims.claim: Under the standard Poisson operator, \(\Phi_{\rm lag}\) has \(\nabla^2\Phi\neq0\) outside the compact matter source, corresponding at first order to an effective dipolar density \(\propto\cos\theta/R^3\) whose dipole moment diverges linearly with box radius
claims.evidence: Same section; analytic calculation plus an uncataloged finite-difference check. This excludes a compact-source Poisson-vacuum interpretation, not every possible local substrate equation
claims.kill: Catalog the finite-difference check as an orrery fixture.

claims.claim: The alternative retarded-direction rule has nonzero curl and admits closed loops with work \(\sim\beta_g GM/R\)
claims.evidence: § Two rules, and only one of them is even a force law; constant-\(R\) circles return zero, while generic loops spanning radius and angle need not
claims.kill: Catalog generic loops spanning radius and angle.

claims.claim: The parent's first-order acceleration contrast is \(2\beta_g\), not \(4\beta_g\), when its declared rule \(\mathbf{a}=-\nabla\Phi\) is used
claims.evidence: § The corrected first-order contrast; the derivation is analytic but not yet represented by an admissible Orrery fixture

claims.claim: Electromagnetism and general relativity cancel the naïve retarded-position aberration for a uniformly moving source, leaving no \(O(\beta_g)\) dipole in the relevant physical interaction
claims.evidence: Sourced 2026-08-28 in [moving-source-gravity-bounds](../../studies/moving-source-gravity-bounds.md) § aberration cancellation: Heaviside/Liénard–Wiechert cancels uniform-motion aberration exactly in electromagnetism; Carlip 2000 shows the quadratic extrapolation in general relativity with residuals at radiation-reaction order. A property of the specific field equations — the control, not a verdict on every preferred-medium equation; [Branch C](branch-c.md) § The control reproduces it inside the model with the odd sector off

claims.claim: In a specified boost-invariant control theory, uniform motion produces no first-order wake; acceleration or explicit boost violation is required for an \(O(\beta_g)\) dipole
claims.evidence: § Why uniform motion does not make a wake in the boost-invariant control; for the minimal class this is now a theorem of the explicit equation ([Branch C](branch-c.md) § The control, eq. 2, even in \(\xi_\parallel\) at every order) — kept at conjecture as a statement about every control theory, which no single equation settles

claims.claim: The delayed-center toy scale \(A_1\sim2\times10^{-3}\) is roughly 50–100× below representative observed disk-lopsidedness scales
claims.evidence: \(\beta_g\approx2\times10^{-3}\) from ~600 km/s; the cited review reports both a larger-sample characteristic scale near 0.1 and older thresholds near 0.2 ([Jog & Combes 2009 review](https://ned.ipac.caltech.edu/level5/Sept09/Jog/Jog2.html), [arXiv:0811.1101](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0811.1101)). The Branch C ceiling is now known and sits at or below this toy scale ([Branch C](branch-c.md) § Walls)

claims.claim: If \(A_1=2\times10^{-3}\) and the foreground is independent zero-mean scatter, a large-\(N\) alignment statistic could measure it
claims.evidence: Moot: Branch C closed (ORB-11175). The surviving Branch C ceiling is \(A_1\lesssim10^{-3}\) to \(3\times10^{-5}\) ([Branch C](branch-c.md) § Walls), so the toy amplitude has no surviving model and the required sample scales to \(\sim10^{7}\) galaxies at the tight reading. § Idealized detectability arithmetic stands as arithmetic; the catalog-error, correlated-structure, and null-correlation debts are no longer owed by this family
claims.kill: Moot: Branch C closed. Would need a reopened branch (daniel_reopen) supplying an amplitude above the ephemeris ceiling before any alignment statistic is owed.

claims.claim: Standard structure formation may correlate peculiar velocity with an \(m=1\) asymmetry axis, confounding an alignment test
claims.evidence: § A degeneracy to measure, not assume — the common-cause intuition is plausible, but the leading tidal tensor is quadrupolar and does not by itself establish an \(m=1\) phase correlation. Moot for this family: Branch C closed (ORB-11175)

claims.claim: A boost-violating model may produce an orientation-dependent split between in-plane lopsidedness and vertical displacement or warping
claims.evidence: Moot: Branch C closed (ORB-11175). For the minimal equation the split does exist in form — the in-plane component of \(\mathbf{w}\) gives the tangential \(m=1\) force and the perpendicular component a midplane vertical acceleration falling as \(1/R\), a bowl-like differential forcing ([Branch C](branch-c.md) § The first-order moving-source solution) — but at amplitudes the ephemeris floor caps below \(10^{-3}\), so the disk-response derivation is no longer owed
claims.kill: Moot: Branch C closed. Reopening needs an amplitude above the ephemeris ceiling.

claims.claim: A conventionally coupled subluminal gravitational mode is tightly constrained by gravitational Cherenkov losses
claims.evidence: Sourced 2026-08-28 in [moving-source-gravity-bounds](../../studies/moving-source-gravity-bounds.md) § gravitational Cherenkov: Moore & Nelson 2001 give \(c-c_g<2\times10^{-15}c\) for Galactic cosmic-ray origins and ~\(2\times10^{-19}c\) for extragalactic; scope is a conventionally coupled mode. The Branch C potential is exactly such a mode, so the bound pins its speed parameter ([Branch C](branch-c.md) § Walls; the scalar-mode extension of the graviton scaling is flagged there as conjecture)

claims.claim: A tracer prediction is uninterpretable until the substrate model specifies all velocity-dependent couplings
claims.evidence: § The gravitomagnetic gap — electromagnetism supplies a warning, not a proof that an unknown substrate has the same cancellation. The minimal Branch C equation has no velocity-dependent force at all; that is a debt of any completion ([moving-source-gravity-bounds](../../studies/moving-source-gravity-bounds.md) § frame dragging), not of the breaking parameters, and is moot with the branch closed

claims.claim: Branch C is not adjudicated by the Poisson-vacuum calculation
claims.evidence: True when written, refuted by adjudication (ORB-11175, 2026-09-04): [Branch C](branch-c.md) writes the explicit boost-violating equation — three breaking parameters at linear, local, two-derivative order — derives its first-order moving-source solution against the Heaviside/Carlip control, maps each parameter onto the sourced walls, and closes the branch: the speed parameter makes no dipole, the source-delay parameter is a rigid offset the solar system excludes, and the dissipative parameter's dipole is locked to a self-acceleration the ephemeris floor ([solar-system-ephemeris-precision-floor](../../studies/solar-system-ephemeris-precision-floor.md)) caps at \(A_1\lesssim10^{-3}\)
claims.kill: Fired: the explicit equation was written and its parameters are already bounded once couplings are specified.
claims.comparator: A specified boost-invariant control (Heaviside/Carlip cancellation), not the delayed-center shortcut.

claims.claim: At linear, local, two-derivative order with one preferred unit vector \(U^\mu\), the boost-violating scalar substrate sector has exactly three breaking parameters — speed \(c_g\ne c\), aether-frame dissipation \(\Gamma\), and source delay \(\tau_s\) — only the two time-odd ones can produce an \(O(\beta_g)\) dipole, and with them off the equation gives the Heaviside form, even in \(\xi_\parallel\) at every order in \(\beta_g\) for every \(c_g\)
claims.evidence: [Branch C](branch-c.md) § The minimal equation and § The control (eqs. 1–2); the Heaviside residual is symbolically zero but the check is uncataloged. The cancellation it reproduces is the sourced control of [moving-source-gravity-bounds](../../studies/moving-source-gravity-bounds.md)
claims.kill: Catalog the branch-c-first-order-solution fixture (gate i). A fourth linear local two-derivative structure built from U, or an O(β_g) dipole from the time-even sector, refutes the count.

claims.claim: For the dissipative parameter the uniformly moving point-source solution is \(\Phi=-(GM/r)\exp[-A_1(r)(1+\cos\theta)]\) with \(A_1(r)=\beta_g r/2\ell_\Gamma\): a first-order potential dipole growing linearly with radius and independent of central concentration, a first-order tangential force \(g_0A_1\sin\theta\) toward the trailing side, and no first-order leading/trailing radial contrast; the source-delay parameter gives a rigid offset \(\tau_s\mathbf{w}\) with \(A_1=\lvert\tau_s\rvert w/r\)
claims.evidence: [Branch C](branch-c.md) § The first-order moving-source solution (eqs. 3–5); PDE residual and both expansions symbolically checked, uncataloged. This is the \(A_1=F(\epsilon_{\rm boost},\beta_g,\rho,\text{tracer coupling})\) map this document owed
claims.kill: Catalog the branch-c-first-order-solution fixture (gates ii–iii): A_1/(kr/2) → 1, radial contrast ∝ k², tangential force → g_0 A_1 sin θ, uniform and Plummer exteriors agree to O(a/r).

claims.claim: The dissipative parameter that sets the dipole also sets a first-order self-acceleration \(\mathbf{a}_{\rm self}=-\tfrac{2}{3}\Gamma\,(\lvert W\rvert/Mc^2)\,\mathbf{w}\) of every gravitationally bound body along its substrate-relative velocity, so a galactic dipole \(A_1\) at radius \(R\) forces \(a_{\rm self}=\tfrac{4A_1}{3R}(\lvert W\rvert/M)(\beta_{\rm b}/\beta_{\rm gal})\) on every other body
claims.evidence: [Branch C](branch-c.md) § The drag lemma (eqs. 6–8): two integrations by parts from the first-order field equation, agreeing with the dissipated-power balance; the integration-by-parts identity verified on a periodic grid to \(10^{-12}\) for a uniform sphere, uncataloged
claims.kill: Catalog the branch-c-first-order-solution fixture (gate iv): self-force on the uniform sphere = −(2k/3)(3/5)GM²/a and on the Plummer sphere = −(2k/3)|W| within grid error.

claims.claim: An explicitly boost-violating local substrate equation yields a galactic \(m=1\) dipole at an observable amplitude — at or above the delayed-center toy scale \(2\times10^{-3}\), let alone the observed lopsidedness scale ~0.1 — with breaking parameters that survive the sourced walls
claims.evidence: **Closed (ORB-11175, [Branch C](branch-c.md) § Walls and § Closure):** of the three breaking parameters, the speed makes no dipole and is pinned by Cherenkov ([moving-source-gravity-bounds](../../studies/moving-source-gravity-bounds.md)); the source delay is a rigid offset the Sun's dynamical centre excludes at \(A_1<4\times10^{-12}\); the dissipative parameter's dipole is locked to a first-order self-acceleration of the Sun of at least \(0.31\,\Gamma\) m/s² in a fixed inertial direction, which the house ephemeris floor ([solar-system-ephemeris-precision-floor](../../studies/solar-system-ephemeris-precision-floor.md), Saturn \(3\times10^{-13}\) to Uranus \(3\times10^{-14}\) m/s²) caps at \(\ell_\Gamma>10\)–\(100\) kpc and hence \(A_1(10\,{\rm kpc})\lesssim10^{-3}\) to \(3\times10^{-5}\) — \(10^{2}\)–\(3\times10^{3}\) below the observed scale on every reading. The four walls named on the card ([lorentz-violation-bounds](../../studies/lorentz-violation-bounds.md), [scalar-gravity-ppn-constraints](../../studies/scalar-gravity-ppn-constraints.md)) bind the completion, not the dissipative parameter. Velocity scales: [lorentz-violation-bounds](../../studies/lorentz-violation-bounds.md), [milky-way-rotation-curve](../../studies/milky-way-rotation-curve.md); universality of the source equation: [source-side-universality-of-g](../../studies/source-side-universality-of-g.md)
claims.kill: Fired 2026-09-04 on the solar-system self-acceleration wall.
claims.comparator: The specified boost-invariant control (Heaviside/Carlip, eq. 2 of the chapter) in the substrate frame; the solar-system confrontation is against the Newtonian-omission ephemeris floor, not a Galilean U+v picture.
